title: Culinary Students at Academy High Blend Learning with Service - NewsBreak
text:
By Elizabeth Dzina No media credit provided. ,
8 hours ago
Little River Academy, TX ( FOX 44 ) — Culinary students at Academy High School are taking their skills beyond the classroom, serving the community as part of their hands-on learning experience.
From preparing meals to giving back, the program blends education with service in a way that benefits the students and those they serve.
Culinary students cooked and served their food to Little River Academy senior citizens and the community with the experience they learned over the years.
“Our classes are usually layered with intro students, culinary students, and advanced students because we like to empower our students to work peer-to-peer with us as a guide on the side,” Culinary Art Teacher Elise Peek Jacko explained.
Fourth-year practicum culinary student Myraa Ward said the class has provided her friends who feel like family, and skills that she’ll use for a lifetime.
“Another thing I would say is the skills they teach you,” Ward said. “The knife skills, communication. Because at first I was shy, and so culinary taught me to, like, open up more, even getting out of my comfort zone. So now I’m, like, an outgoing person.”
Brady Vanwagenen, a fourth-year practicum culinary student, said he started cooking before high school because of his dad.
“I’m planning on culinary school, the Culinary Institute of America in New York, hopefully, and just hopefully become a top chef,” Vanwagenen stated.
Vanwagenen said his dream is to own a Michelin-star restaurant and go on the popular cooking show Master Chef .
“I would go on Master Chef ,” Vanwagenen said. “That would be a fun experience. Even if I lost, it would just give me more experience in the stressfulness of all of it. And it’d just be really fun. If I won, it would be just way better.”
Academy High School culinary students are building cooking skills while learning service and teamwork beyond the classroom.
